sec: GLUT transporters, C-peptide and incretin hormones

items.q: Match the transporter to the tissue location — 1) GLUT1 2) GLUT2 3) GLUT3 4) GLUT4 … A) Brain, kidney, colon, placenta, erythrocyte B) Liver, pancreatic beta cell, small intestine, kidney C) Brain, kidney, placenta D) Heart, skeletal muscle, adipose tissue
items.exp: The GLUT table gives the listed tissue distributions for GLUT1, GLUT2, GLUT3 and GLUT4. (Book p928)

items.q: Which transporter is marked as insulin-stimulated uptake of glucose?
items.exp: The GLUT4 row states insulin-stimulated uptake of glucose. (Book p928)

items.q: The small-intestine transporter that takes up fructose is ___.
items.exp: The GLUT5 row lists small intestine and uptake of fructose. (Book p928)

items.q: Assess the transporter table: I SGLT1 is in small intestine and actively takes up glucose from the lumen. II SGLT2 reabsorbs glucose in the proximal convoluted tubule of the kidney.
items.exp: Both SGLT rows carry those tissue and function labels. (Book p928)

items.q: Match the glucose/C-peptide pattern to the associated condition — 1) C-peptide undetectable, glucose increased 2) C-peptide increased, glucose increased 3) C-peptide increased, glucose decreased 4) C-peptide decreased, glucose decreased … A) T1DM B) T2DM C) Insulinoma D) Exogenous insulin
items.exp: The table pairs undetectable C-peptide/increased glucose with T1DM, increased/increased with T2DM, increased/decreased with insulinoma, and decreased/decreased with exogenous insulin. (Book p928)

items.q: A patient has low glucose, low C-peptide and a history suggesting administered insulin. Which association is printed?
items.exp: The C-peptide table associates decreased C-peptide and decreased glucose with exogenous insulin. (Book p928)

items.q: How many incretin hormones are branched from the word 'incretins' in the diagram?
items.exp: The diagram branches incretins to GLP-1 and GIP, making two hormones. (Book p928)

items.q: The incretin effect augments insulin production in response to which type of meal entry named on the page?
opts: A fat meal entering the stomach
A protein meal entering the colon
A saline meal entering the ileum
items.exp: The note says incretins augment insulin production in response to a glucose meal, written as intrajejunal glucose. (Book p928)

items.q: Which recombinant GLP-1 application is written as not easily degraded by DPP-4?
opts: Recombinant GLP-1 used in treatment of DM
items.exp: The applied-aspect note names recombinant GLP-1 for DM and says it is not easily degraded by DPP-4. (Book p928)

items.q: Assess the applied-aspect list: I Exenatide is annotated with pancreatitis risk. II Liraglutide is written as subcutaneous.
items.exp: The page lists exenatide with pancreatitis risk and liraglutide s/c. (Book p928)

items.q: Match the applied drug to the page's note — 1) Exenatide 2) Liraglutide 3) Semaglutide 4) Tirzepatide … A) Pancreatitis risk B) Subcutaneous C) Oral with increased weight loss D) Dual GLP-1/GIP analogue
items.exp: The application list gives exenatide with pancreatitis risk, liraglutide s/c, oral semaglutide with increased weight loss, and tirzepatide as a dual GLP-1/GIP analogue. (Book p928)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among the abbreviated hormones or transporters explicitly written in the incretin section?
items.exp: GLP-1, GIP and DPP-4 appear in this page's incretin notes; cortisol does not. (Book p928)
